completed_stage_receipts.summary: Confirmed control-plane defects from the audit: stale external monitor-liveness representation and, later in validation, a manifest/proof version lifecycle conflict.

Classified two systemic failure classes: external-product-observation-staleness and task-mutation-version-coupled-to-formal-meta-proof-version. Both affect Universal control truth, not BUSINESS truth.

Mapped live automation state, repository observation/cache surfaces, task manifest mutation/CAS versioning, lease takeover, formal meta-proof lifecycle and CI closure. BUSINESS owners/leases remain out of scope.

History search found the proof-version defect already occurred at V53 and was repaired by generating a current-version formal meta closure on takeover. The same class recurred after that accepted fix because the newer controller correctly forbids fabricating incomplete maintenance as completed proof. Escalated from component-level takeover repair to system-architecture lifecycle separation. Monitor liveness likewise escalates from peer-watch mitigation to external-state authority separation.

Used current runtime, unchanged regression, prior accepted takeover repair and live CI failure as the learning set. The evidence shows the earlier equality invariant had a useful anti-staleness goal but now conflates task mutation chronology with formal proof chronology.
Reused the existing task mutation counter, meta verifier, controller and regression suite. No new proof service, supervisor, registry or protocol axis is required.

Rejected rolling back manifest_version takeover increments and rejected repeating the V53 pattern of manufacturing a formal meta-run on every takeover. Accepted lifecycle decoupling: latest completed formal run may target an older manifest mutation version, but never a future one, and must still structurally PASS.

Verified autonomously that acquire_resume_lease increments manifest_version, the regression requires exact equality, and the handoff intentionally leaves formal V61 proof historical while newer task state exists. No user design decision is needed to remove this internal contradiction.

No account/startup instruction change. The correct control surface is the repository proof-binding regression plus explicit task-manifest/handoff semantics; prompt text cannot resolve lifecycle coupling.

Design keeps one manifest mutation counter and one latest completed formal proof pointer. It changes the relation from equality to non-future binding plus structural validity, retains strict takeover versioning, adds no authority surface and removes pressure to create redundant meta artifacts on every lease takeover.

Deletes the recurrent workaround requirement 'new formal meta-run for every manifest_version bump' while preserving anti-staleness checks: proof ref exists, schema matches, run structurally passes, and its target cannot exceed current durable task version. Net architecture is simpler and more truthful.

Implemented proof lifecycle decoupling by replacing exact current-manifest equality with non-future target binding plus unchanged structural evaluation of the latest completed meta run. Retained acquire_resume_lease version advancement. Also corrected monitor liveness representation in the task manifest so external scheduler state requires live product reread and user-deleted monitors are not recreated without authorization.

Fresh hosted validation passed the risk-tiered control-plane audit, Agent architecture harness and complete pytest suite after the proof-lifecycle repair. This follows two earlier real CI failures that were used to reopen and strengthen the implementation rather than being ignored.

reopen_history.reason: Hosted CI run 38275331371 failed because compacting the manifest removed a required methodology contract field; implementation was reopened and the field restored.

Second hosted CI run 38275584909 proved a deeper pre-existing architecture conflict between legal manifest_version advancement and exact formal meta-run target equality; history search found the same class in V53, requiring abstraction escalation rather than another same-level current-version meta artifact.
